details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned that the tokenization of financial assets and liabilities is a structural shift, not merely a payments technology upgrade, that could profoundly reshape how global financial markets settle transactions, manage liquidity, and absorb risk. Tobias Adrian, Director of the IMF's Monetary and Capital Markets Department, emphasized that policy decisions made now will determine whether tokenization strengthens or fragments the financial system, highlighting the need for clear rules on ownership, settlement, and jurisdiction. The IMF identified three emerging forms of digital money: tokenized bank deposits, stablecoins, and tokenized central bank reserves, each presenting unique opportunities and challenges.

title: IMF Warns Tokenization Could Reshape Global Financial System

details: The Eurosystem's T2 real-time gross settlement system, which processes over ‐2 trillion in wholesale euro payments daily, experienced an incident on July 6, disrupting the start of the settlement window for euro and Danish Krone transactions. The system shifted into a non-optional maintenance mode, queuing payment instructions. This marks the second such incident within a week following a June 2026 system update, which integrated ISO 20022 standards. The European Central Bank (ECB) has indicated operational resilience and cybersecurity concerns are paramount, with an investigation into the root cause underway.
title: ECB's T2 Payment System Experiences Disruption

details: As of July 1, 2026, the transitional period for the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation has ended. This marks a significant shift for crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) operating within the EU, as firms are now required to hold a MiCA license to legally serve customers. The regulation aims to standardize crypto-asset rules across the EU, enhance market integrity, and ensure consumer protection by imposing requirements on transparency, disclosure, authorization, and supervision of transactions.
title: EU MiCA Regulation Transitional Period Concludes

details: At the ECB's annual conference in Sintra, central bankers globally expressed significant concerns about how artificial intelligence (AI) will impact the world economy and financial stability. Discussions highlighted AI's potential to disrupt financial and labor markets, inflate and crash asset bubbles at high speed, and complicate bank lending and supervision. While AI offers efficiency gains, officials fear its disruptive capacity, including the creation of unforeseen problems and the amplification of existing risks, making regulatory oversight a significant challenge.
title: Central Bankers Express Concerns Over AI's Economic Impact

details: Perpetual futures, often referred to as "perps" in crypto markets, are growing in popularity, particularly in offshore trading environments. These derivatives allow traders to speculate on the future price of an asset without an expiry date, offering continuous exposure and leverage. The increasing adoption of perps is impacting traditional futures exchanges by providing an alternative, often more liquid, and accessible venue for cryptocurrency price speculation, raising questions about market structure and regulatory oversight.
title: Perpetual Futures Gaining Traction in Offshore Crypto Trading
